answer: Behavioral kernel divergence scoring. Each identity's action history is compressed into a low-dimensional kernel density over timing, task mix, and counterpart choice; clusters of identities whose kernels are near-duplicates are flagged post hoc. A real agent's usage vine branches idiosyncratically, while clones stay tightly correlated. Flagged clusters lose accrued reputation and payout eligibility pending review, so an attacker must either diversify each clone's genuine behavior at real operating cost or see the whole canyon of accounts devalued at once.
